Opposite Party/s

 Appearance :
 For the Petitioner/s : Mr. Mrityunjay Kumar, Advocate
 For the Opposite Party/s : Mr. Uma Shankar Prasad Singh, App
 ======================================================
 Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Rajesh Kumar Verma
 Oral Order
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State.

Petitioner seeks bail, who is in custody since 18.08.2022 in connection with Mahila P.S. Case No. 89 of 2021, F.I.R. dated 16.12.2021 for the offences punishable under Sections 448, 341, 342, 504, 323,
506, 376/34 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 4/6 of POCSO Act.
According to prosecution case, as per written report of the informant stating therein that the petitioner was keeping evil eye on her and sexually harassed several times in past.

On 12.12.2021 at 02 P.M. when the parents of informant were not present in the house and the victim was alone in her house, accused Bahzad barged into her house through window and pressed the mouth of victim and then committed forcible rape Patna High Court CR.
When the victim raised alarm, the neighbors assembled and accused was apprehended red handed.

Thereafter, the brother of Md. Bahzad, Md. Faiyaj, Md. Aksad, Md. Ibrahim, Md.
Rehamajuddin, Md. Saiyad and Md. Mozil reached at the house of victim carrying lathi, danda,
Farsa, Garasa in their hands.
They abused the victim and threatened her to kill her throwing acid.
They took out the accused from the house and also threatened to make the video of her viral.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that petitioner has clean antecedent and he has falsely been implicated in the present case.

He further submits that petitioner has not committed any Md. Bahzad vs The State Of Bihar on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46866087/
1 offence as alleged in the F.I.R. and the in fact the petitioner and the victim girl was in love.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State has vehemently opposed the prayer for bail of the petitioner on the basis of material available on record and case diary submits that the statement of the victim girl was recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. in which she has categorically stated that the petitioner has committed rape upon her.
He further submits that the victim girl was minor at the time of occurrence.
Considering the aforesaid facts, I am not inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail in connection with Mahila P.S. Patna High Court CR.
